t308b: The three principles of the anti-violence programme
d5p1: From the very beginning, the Link-Italia Project has consistently proposed, within the Zooanthropological LINK Approach, an Interpretation of Animal Abuse and/or Killing structured in 5 Dimensions, as set out below.
d5p2: The Violence Graduation Hypothesis, Deviance Generalization Hypothesis, Antecedent Lifestyle Hypothesis and Multi-Offensive Conduct Hypothesis (F. Sorcinelli 2026) are interpretative tools that allow the «phenomenon» to be analysed from different angles, revealing the plurality of paths through which animal abuse and/or killing may arise, develop, become part of a broader antisocial and/or criminal conduct, or be traced back to previous experiences and conditions of vulnerability.
d5p3: Only an integrated, non-polarised view of these Hypotheses can fully grasp the intrinsic complexity of the LINK Phenomenon.
d5p4: A complexity perfectly expressed in the definition formulated by the Link-Italia Project, which frames animal abuse and killing as an offence to be countered in itself, yet not as an isolated «phenomenon», but as a systemic and multidimensional indicator.
d5p5: Therefore animal abuse and/or killing, with reference to the Violence Graduation Hypothesis, Deviance Generalization Hypothesis, Antecedent Lifestyle Hypothesis and the Multi - Offensive Conduct Hypothesis (F. Sorcinelli 2026) [1], must be interpreted as:
d5l1: Acts to be prevented, treated, prosecuted and countered in themselves, without limiting the analysis to the «effects» of the conduct, but addressing the «phenomenon» of violence and/or antisociality (F. Sorcinelli 2026) [2] [3]. Moreover, animals, as sentient beings, are declared subjects of direct protection both in the Italian Constitution (art. 9) and in the very recent “Save Animals Law” (6 June 2025, no. 82).
d5l2: Symptoms of a pathogenic existential situation in the person who commits the abuse (Antecedent Lifestyle Hypothesis); in particular, if committed by children or adolescents, this refers to a family or environmental situation marked by physical, psychological or sexual abuse, neglect, inadequate care, excessive care; by these forms of violence together or by states of harm such as educational neglect and/or inadequate care (F. Sorcinelli, 2006) (3).
d5l3: Specific Indicators of Social Dangerousness (Violence Graduation Hypothesis), i.e. indicators of concurrent, or predictive of subsequent, other deviant, antisocial and/or criminal conduct) such as (F. Ascione, 1993) [4]:
d5l3b:
• Acts of destruction - vandalism and/or arson.
  • Aggression - deliberate psychological and/or physical cruelty towards people.
  • Thefts involving a victim – pickpocketing, extortion, armed robbery.
  • Kidnapping, sexual violence, assault, with particular regard to the phenomenon of spree killers and mass murder, homicide, with particular regard to the phenomenon of serial killers.
d5l4: Co-occurring Phenomena (Deviance Generalization Hypothesis) of a broader pattern of deviant, antisocial and/or criminal conduct, previous or concurrent.
d5l5: An Integral Part of other crimes (Multi-Offensive Conduct Hypothesis) such as: persecutory acts; stalking; bullying, cyberbullying, intimidation (in Italy especially of a mafia type); domestic violence against women, minors, the elderly and vulnerable groups in general; stalking, sectarian crimes; drug dealing; predatory crimes; sexual crimes, homicide; etc.
d5p6: NB: For descriptive purposes and ease of analysis, in the LINK Tetralogy (2026) Francesca Sorcinelli defines this last scenario as the Ipotesi della Condotta Plurioffensiva or, to use a more international term, the Multi-Offensive Conduct Hypothesis.

pp03: We exist to train the Professional and the Citizen of the Third Millennium for the role of Active Safeguard in the prevention, treatment and countering of any deviant, antisocial and/or criminal conduct, to protect any Member of the Social Community (People and Animals) through the Anti-Violence Programme to which the We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare®. Certified Company and We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare®. Certified Professional Certifications belong
pp04: For the first time worldwide (2026), we define the Certified Company Certification Standards and Certified Professional, belonging to the We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare® Anti-Violence Programme, as fundamental, cutting-edge Criteria for assessing how Companies, Organisations, Associations, Institutions, Bodies, Professionals, manage Environmental, Social and Governance issues, as they are aligned with the SDGs (Sustainable, Development and Goals) and made up of indicators consistent with CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility), PSR (Public Social Responsability) and ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) Policies.
pp05: New Criteria that enable Public or Private Bodies and Professionals to play an ever greater leading role in building a Sustainable Future, as it has a Positive and Proactive Social Impact.
pp06: CSR / PSR Criteria and ESG Criteria describe a Company, Organisation, Association, Body or Institution according to non-financial parameters, while enhancing its Social and Environmental reach.
pp07: Being sustainable for the “Enterprise” means making an investment that creates a virtuous circle between economic growth and the well-being of people and the planet.
pp08: The prevention, treatment and countering of the LINK Phenomenon express par excellence the ability to combine the main dimensions of Environmental and Social Sustainability, implementing the virtuous circle between economic growth and the well-being of people and the planet, through the introduction of the One Safety, One Health, One Welfare® Trinomial and of the People - Animals Binomial
pp09: After all, Public or Private Bodies, besides being workplaces, are Centres of Aggregation where people spend most of their time. A container of humanity where culture is created and spread through values, messages and models that are passed on far beyond the walls of the Company, Organisation or Association itself.
pp10: We are Partners who support Public or Private Bodies and Professionals in fulfilling Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) or Public Social Responsibility (PSR) relating to the Person - Animal Binomial, from a Zooanthropologically oriented LINK perspective, through the Anti-Violence Programme belonging to the We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare®. Certified Company and We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare®. Certified Professional Certifications
pp11: We enable our Partners to produce an important Social Report whose authority is anchored to a Certification that attests to their undertaking in terms of commitment and concrete actions.
pp12: Developing and sharing knowledge to prepare Public or Private Bodies, Professionals and Citizens to play an Active Role in the prevention, treatment and countering of violence against every Member (People and Animals) of their own Community, through a vision of Interspecific Professionalism and Active Citizenship, is our Mission!
pp15: Correlation between animal abuse and/or killing, interpersonal violence and any other deviant, antisocial and/or criminal conduct (Francesca Sorcinelli, Link-Italia Project, 2006)
pp17: An integrated, unifying approach that aims to sustainably balance and optimise the health of people, animals and ecosystems. It recognises that the health of humans, domestic and wild animals, plants and the environment are closely linked and interdependent (OHHLEP).
pp19:
For us there is no One Health, One Welfare, without One Safety
One Safety, One Health, One Welfare®
pp20: Interpersonal violence is one of the major public health problems worldwide (WHO 2002). Antisocial conduct causes 1.3 million deaths every year and an even greater number of injuries (WHO and UN 2014), which is why: “preventing, treating and countering interpersonal violence is a matter of life or death. In this framework, preventing, treating and countering violence against animals, as a duty in itself, is what can make the difference between human life and death (LINK), and preventing, treating and countering interpersonal violence, in its correlations (LINK), is what can make the difference between animal life and death” (F. Sorcinelli, Link-Italia Project, 2006).
pp21:

pp22: Until the Zooanthropologically oriented LINK Approach is adopted, the prevention, treatment and countering of violence against the Members of the Social Community (People and Animals) will remain disconnected, inefficient and ineffective.
pp23: The We Break THE LINK® - One Safety, One Health, One Welfare® Anti-Violence Programme develops in two complementary directions:
pp24: We create a shared Specialist and Social Culture on the Prevention, Treatment and Countering of the LINK Phenomenon, through Training Paths to develop Professional Sensitivity (Level I) or Specialist Skills (Level II) for Practitioners and Social Skills (Level I) for Citizens.
